title: Child Windows and Scrolling
summary: A child window is a scrolling region inside a window - a list that scrolls while the buttons below it stay put, or a two-pane layout. This lesson covers `BeginChild`, sizing children to fill space, scrolling from code, auto-scrolling logs, and **clipping** so a list of a hundred thousand items costs nothing.
markdown:
## BeginChild

```cpp-norun
ImGui::BeginChild("stones", ImVec2(0, 200), ImGuiChildFlags_Borders);   // full width, 200 high, with a border
for (const Stone& s : stones) ImGui::Text("%s", s.name.c_str());
ImGui::EndChild();                                                       // ALWAYS, like End
if (ImGui::Button("Add")) addStone();                                    // stays below, not scrolled
```

`BeginChild`/`EndChild` follow the **window** rule: `EndChild` is always called, whatever `BeginChild` returned.

Sizes: `0` means "fill what is available", a positive number is a fixed size, a **negative** number means "fill, minus this much". So "a list that fills the window except for one row of buttons below it" is:

```cpp-norun
const float footer = ImGui::GetFrameHeightWithSpacing();      // the height of one row of buttons
ImGui::BeginChild("list", ImVec2(0, -footer), ImGuiChildFlags_Borders);
// ...
ImGui::EndChild();
ImGui::Button("Add");
```

## Two panes side by side

```cpp-norun
ImGui::BeginChild("left", ImVec2(200, 0), ImGuiChildFlags_Borders | ImGuiChildFlags_ResizeX);  // resizable
drawLevelList();
ImGui::EndChild();
ImGui::SameLine();
ImGui::BeginChild("right");                      // takes the rest
drawLevelDetails();
ImGui::EndChild();
```

`ImGuiChildFlags_ResizeX` adds a handle on the child's right edge the user can drag. (Before version 1.90 the second argument of `BeginChild` was a `bool border`; the flags replaced it.)

## Scrolling from code

```cpp-norun
ImGui::SetScrollHereY(0.5f);           // scroll so the current cursor position is in the middle
ImGui::SetScrollY(0.0f);               // to the top
float y = ImGui::GetScrollY(), maxY = ImGui::GetScrollMaxY();
```

A log window wants to **follow** new lines, but only if the user has not scrolled up to read something:

```cpp-norun
const bool atBottom = ImGui::GetScrollY() >= ImGui::GetScrollMaxY();   // measure BEFORE adding lines
for (const auto& line : log) ImGui::TextUnformatted(line.c_str());
if (atBottom) ImGui::SetScrollHereY(1.0f);                              // keep following
```

## Clipping long lists

Drawing 100,000 lines every frame is slow even if only 30 are visible. **`ImGuiListClipper`** works out which items are on screen, so you only draw those, while the scroll bar still behaves as if all of them were there:

```cpp-norun
ImGuiListClipper clipper;
clipper.Begin((int)lines.size());                  // all items have the same height
while (clipper.Step())
    for (int i = clipper.DisplayStart; i < clipper.DisplayEnd; ++i)
        ImGui::TextUnformatted(lines[i].c_str());
```

The idea is simple arithmetic: with each item `h` pixels high, the scroll position `y` and the visible height `H`, the first visible item is `floor(y / h)` and the last is `ceil((y + H) / h)`. The clipper reserves empty space for the items above and below so the scroll bar is right. The practice writes this calculation.

Clipping needs every item to have the **same height**. For variable heights, keep a prefix sum of heights and binary-search it, or group items into rows of equal height.

## Common mistakes

> [!warning] Calling EndChild only when BeginChild returned true
> Like End, EndChild is always called.

> [!warning] Auto-scroll that fights the user
> Check whether you were at the bottom before adding lines, and only follow then.

> [!warning] Drawing every line of a huge log
> Use ImGuiListClipper; the cost then depends on the window height, not the log length.

## Check yourself
```quiz
? What does a negative child size mean?
- The child is hidden until the user scrolls to it
+ Fill the available space minus that amount, leaving room for widgets after the child
- A fixed size measured from the right or bottom edge of the screen
> 0 fills all the space, a positive number is a fixed size, and a negative one fills minus that much.

? How does ImGuiListClipper make a huge list cheap?
+ It computes which equal-height items are visible from the scroll position and draws only those, while reserving space for the rest
- It draws every item once into a texture and reuses the texture each frame
- It draws a different slice of the list each frame, so the whole list is drawn over many frames
> Only the visible items are drawn, so the cost depends on the window height, not the list length, and the scroll bar still behaves as if all items were there.

? How do you make a log follow new lines without fighting the user?
- Call SetScrollHereY(1.0f) every frame after drawing the lines
- Call SetScrollY(0.0f) each time a new line is added
+ Scroll to the bottom only if it was already at the bottom
> Check whether the scroll is at the bottom before adding lines. Scrolling down every frame drags the user away from whatever they scrolled up to read.

? A child should fill the window except for 40 pixels of buttons below it. What height do you pass?
- 40
+ -40
- 0
> Negative sizes mean "fill, minus this much"; 0 would fill everything and push the buttons out of view.

? What must be true of the items for ImGuiListClipper to work?
- They are sorted
- There are fewer than 1000 of them
+ They all have the same height
> It computes the visible range from a fixed item height. For variable heights you need a prefix sum of heights instead.

? With items 20 pixels high, scrolled to y = 1000, what is the first visible item?
- 20
+ 50
- 1000
- 51
> floor(1000 / 20) = 50, counting items from 0.
```

- Make a log window with 50,000 generated lines, a clipper, and auto-scroll that stops when you scroll up.
